title: Houses 2/9: Porphyry, Sripati, Meridian, Morinus, Carter (O/S/X/M/F)
description:
### Summary
Add the quadrant-arithmetic and equatorial-projection house systems: Porphyry (O), Sripati (S), Meridian/axial (X), Morinus (M), Carter (F). Porphyry is the universal polar-circle fallback used by later iterative systems, so it MUST land here. This task also first exercises the driver-level finite-difference cusp-speed path (`do_interpol`) added in sub-task 1, via S/X/M/F.

### Files
- `src/houses.rs` — replace the stub match arms for O/S/X/M/F in `calc_h`; add a reusable `fn fill_porphyry(h: &mut CalcH, geolat, sine, cose, do_speed)` helper (later sub-tasks call it on polar failure).
- `tests/c-gen/gen_houses.c` — add a `"quad_arith"` JSON key.
- `tests/golden-data/houses.json` — regenerate.
- `tests/golden/houses.rs` — add a `quad_arith` test.

### Implementation steps
Read `docs/c-ref-houses.md` §5 "O", "S", "X", "M", "F" and §4.2(b),(d),(e).
1. **Porphyry (O)** — ref §5 "O". Extract the body into `fill_porphyry(...)` so the iterative systems (sub-task 4) can `goto porphyry` by calling it. Re-assert `cusps[1]=ac; cusps[10]=mc` at the top (repairs a corrupted prior attempt). Cusp speeds: §4.2(b) linear quadrant-rate interpolation (NOT AscDash): `q1_speed = ac_speed - mc_speed; cusp_speed[2]=ac_speed - q1_speed/3; [3]=ac_speed - q1_speed/3*2; [11]=ac_speed + q1_speed/3; [12]=ac_speed + q1_speed/3*2`. The post-switch mirror (sub-task 1) fills the opposite cusps.
2. **Sripati (S)** — ref §5 "S": reassigns `cusps[1]` and `cusps[10]` (half-sector offset from ac/mc). Set `h.do_interpol = true` (finite-diff speeds).
3. **Meridian (X)** — ref §5 "X": 12-iteration `armc_to_mc`-style loop with the rotated index `j = ((i+10-1) mod 12)+1`. Set `h.do_interpol = true`.
4. **Morinus (M)** — ref §5 "M": same equatorial points as X but projected via `crate::math::cotrans([a,0.0,1.0], +ekl)` (note the +ekl sign; verify against the existing cotrans port — cotrans rotates by the given angle; pass `eps.to_radians()` if cotrans expects radians, else degrees — CHECK the signature in src/math.rs:271 before calling). `cusps[j] = result[0]`. Set `h.do_interpol = true`.
5. **Carter (F)** — ref §5 "F": `a = RA of ascendant` via `cotrans([ac,0,1], -ekl)[0]`; loop fills only `i ∈ {2,3,10,11,12}` (the `if i<=3 || i>=10` guard) with the `tand(ra)/cose` MC-style projection. Set `h.do_interpol = true`. cusps[4..9] are filled by the post-switch mirror.

### C reference
`docs/c-ref-houses.md` §5 O/S/X/M/F; §4.2(b)(d)(e); §12.1 (armc_to_mc normalization). Confirm `crate::math::cotrans` signature/units at src/math.rs:271 before steps 4–5.

### Golden tests
- C harness: add key `"quad_arith"` to `gen_houses.c`: for each char in `['O','S','X','M','F']` × the sub-task-1 battery, call `swe_houses_armc_ex2` (cusp_speed/ascmc_speed non-NULL) and emit `{hsys, armc, geolat, eps, cusps:[1..12], cusp_speed:[1..12]}`. Regenerate houses.json with the build/run command from sub-task 1.
- Rust test `quad_arith` in `tests/golden/houses.rs`: assert cusps (eps 1e-9) and cusp_speeds (eps 1e-7). The finite-difference speeds for S/X/M/F will not be bitwise-exact — keep them at 1e-7. Porphyry (O) speeds are analytical — try 1e-9 first.

### Acceptance criteria
- `cargo clippy --all-targets` clean.
- `cargo test --test golden houses::quad_arith -- --nocapture` passes.
- Sub-task-1 tests still pass: `cargo test --test golden houses -- --nocapture`.

### Escape hatch
Same as sub-task 1: stop after two attempts on >1e-8 position mismatches; for FP issues read swehouse.c directly; escalate to Opus. The finite-diff speed path is the likely first failure point — verify `dt`, `darmc`, and the `diff_degrees/2/dt` formula against ref §4.2(d) before assuming a system-formula bug.
execution_record: Implemented O/S/X/M/F per c-ref-houses.md §5. Reused mc_like() for X's per-cusp loop and Carter's loop (both are exactly the tand(x)/cose projection already factored out). Reused cotrans() for M (+eps) and F (-eps) — sign convention confirmed consistent with existing rotate_x_sincos. fill_porphyry() extracted as a standalone fn (cusps/cusp_speeds by &mut, ac/mc/speeds by value, returns possibly-polar-swapped ac) so later iterative systems can call it on Newton-iteration failure. One clippy needless_range_loop fix: Carter's sparse {2,3,10,11,12} cusp set is iterated via an explicit array literal rather than a guarded 2..=12 range. All golden tests passed on first run (cusps 1e-9, cusp_speed 1e-9 for Porphyry analytical / 1e-7 for S,X,M,F finite-diff) — no FP fidelity debugging needed.
